about: The task-shaped set. Two probes per blueprint: one a reader would type into a box, one a
sentence an agent would carry from a user. Written against what each blueprint DOES rather
than what its manifest SAYS, and deliberately avoiding the archive's own vocabulary — the
smoke set beside this one scores identically with the encoder present and absent because
every query there shares content words with its target, which makes it blind to the exact
outage it would be run to catch.
The near-miss groups are the point of the blueprint half. On a sixteen-item corpus recall@5
is won or lost between guarded-merge-bot / guarded-assistant-line / delegation-broker,
between incident-commander / frontline-triage, and between nightly-data-janitor /
schema-forge-etl / checkpoint-resume-runner. Each probe below has to beat its own group.
HELD-OUT HONESTY: the author of these probes had read the corpus. `lexicalOverlap` is
reported per query for that reason — a set that drifts lexically announces itself instead
of quietly becoming the smoke set again.

blueprints.query: two opinions then settle on one
I want two independent attempts at the same question and something to reconcile them into a single answer
cheap model unless it is hard
send easy questions to a small fast model and only pay for the expensive one when it is actually needed
resume after a crash
a long job that saves progress as it goes so a failure halfway through does not mean starting over
hand work to an outside agent
find some third party service that can do this, give it the job, and do not trust what comes back
answer customer tickets
sort incoming customer messages, handle the easy ones automatically, and pass the rest to a person
research with real sources
look something up across several places and keep checking until every statement has evidence behind it
screen what users send the model
put safety checks around a chatbot so nothing unsafe reaches it and nothing unsafe comes back out
review pull requests
have something look at code changes and run the tests, but a person signs off before anything lands
try many ideas and keep the best
produce lots of candidate ideas, score them against each other, and carry the winners forward
handle production alerts
when something breaks in production work out what to do, and get a person involved if it looks risky
overnight data cleanup
a scheduled job that tidies up records every night with nobody watching it
keep work pointed at a goal
one person says what we are trying to achieve and another says how we will know, and the worker must not see the second
monitor a pipeline I already have
add tracing and alerting to a workflow that already exists without rewriting any of it
draft then grade the draft
one thing writes and another grades it, and the writer must never learn what it is being graded on
clean up messy documents
take unstructured files, force them into a fixed shape, and fix whatever fails the check
build a feature end to end
the basic line that plans a change, writes it, tests it, fixes what broke and ships it

cards.query: grade one answer against a rubric
run a python script somewhere it cannot hurt anything
reorder a queue of work as things change
decide what to work on next
score how important a piece of work is
check what an agent actually did step by step
split work across several workers at once
gather the parallel results back together
ask a person to approve before it goes ahead
run the project's tests and say what broke
write the code for the planned change
work out why a test is failing and fix it

negatives.query: book a table for four at an italian restaurant on friday night
how do I convert celsius to fahrenheit
what is the capital of portugal
remind me to call my mother on sunday
